findings.claim: Concept anchor `<!-- concept: foresight-test -->` on the Q4 substitution entry (the same anchor already heads Concept 5, the foresight test).
findings.failure_mode: concept anchor names the wrong concept; the concept-index will route 'foresight-test' lookups to the substitution entry and 'substitution-test' lookups nowhere in this file
findings.evidence: Deep 72-80: Q4 is the substitution test, distinct from Q3 foresight (deep 62-70). Sibling distillations (aar line 22, software-business line 30) anchor this concept as `substitution-test`.

findings.claim: Signal: "Q4 is being treated as requiring all three sub-questions to be No"; diagnosis: disjunction misread.
findings.failure_mode: signal states the correct reading as the misreading; the follow-up in the same row then asks to confirm all three are No, which is what the source requires to proceed
findings.evidence: Deep 80: 'Yes to any of 4a, 4b, or 4c routes to Recommendation E; No to all three routes to Q5.' Requiring all three No to proceed is the source's rule; the misread is requiring all three Yes before routing to E.
findings.fix: correct: Signal: "Q4 is being treated as requiring all three sub-questions to be Yes before routing away from the individual"

findings.claim: LFUO provides the broader framework "that the NHS guide's per-individual decision fits within. Use NHS for the individual-action filter; use LFUO for the organisational learning framework that surrounds it."
findings.failure_mode: nests the individual-action decision inside a framework that explicitly walls itself off from administrative action
findings.evidence: LFUO deep 7 and 53 confirm the four tools (AAR, RLS, FLA, Learning Review). LFUO deep 67 [V]: 'It is critical to maintain a solid firewall between the FLA and any potential administrative actions that may be taken against the employee'; excluded actions include 'any type of disciplinary actions and other adverse actions such as forced retraining'. The NHS G branch can route to individual training and disciplinary processes (NHS deep 144).
findings.fix: correct: "LFUO provides the multi-tool learning framework (AAR, RLS, FLA, Learning Review) and keeps a firewall between its learning reviews and any administrative action. Use LFUO for the organisational learning; use NHS for the separate management conversation about an individual action, kept apart from the learning review as LFUO requires."

findings.section: Integration with Other References (OpenStax Business Ethics)
findings.claim: "OpenStax, Business Ethics (Ch 7) | OB frames moral minimum, ethical minimum, and ethical maximum. The NHS guide's wider-investigation directive on every branch is the ethical-maximum response; the individual response is the minimum."
findings.failure_mode: wrong source label ('OB'), wrong chapter, and a forced mapping onto Business Ethics' terms
findings.evidence: Business Ethics deep 107: ethical maximum/minimum at Ch 3.1 ('Ethical Responsibilities Often Extend Beyond Legal Requirements'); deep 146: moral minimum at Ch 4 ('Key Terms'). Not Ch 7. Ethical minimum is 'the least a company might do' in a situation; nothing in either deep ref equates the individual response with it.
findings.fix: correct: "OpenStax, Business Ethics (Ch 3.1, Ch 4) | Business Ethics distinguishes the moral minimum, ethical minimum and ethical maximum. Read the NHS guide's pairing of any individual response with a wider investigation as going beyond the minimum response to an incident (a distillation-level reading)."

findings.claim: Reason: "the guide draws on Reason's work implicitly throughout its system-default prior."
findings.failure_mode: characterises the borrowed-through lineage beyond what the source states
findings.evidence: Deep 165: 'no specific work or concept of Reason's is cited by name'. Deep 182: 'any further characterisation of either lineage is outside the scope of this deep reference because it is not stated in the source.'
findings.fix: strip: end the bullet at "No specific concept or work is cited by name in the source body."
